title: RegInsight purpose and chatbot
keywords: reginsight assistant chatbot capabilities model training fine tuned trained agents
text: RegInsight AI supports inspection analysis, recurring risk discovery and source-linked human review. The chatbot uses a locally hosted Qwen model with RegInsight instructions and retrieved project evidence. Its base weights have not been fine-tuned on the inspection dataset. Domain configuration and retrieval are different from model training. The inspection investigation agent and the chatbot agent are separate components. The chatbot does not change records or make regulatory decisions.

title: Inspection classifications
keywords: NAI VAI OAI meaning classification official action voluntary action
text: NAI means No Action Indicated. VAI means Voluntary Action Indicated. OAI means Official Action Indicated: FDA describes this as a recommendation for regulatory or administrative action. Say recommended, not required or guaranteed. These are inspection outcome classifications. Unknown classifications are kept separate. In RegInsight, OAI rate divides OAI inspections by inspections with known classifications; it is not the percentage of observation rows.

title: Observation themes and severity
keywords: category tag tagging severity high critical low medium themes observations
text: Observation text is tagged with a theme, category, severity, confidence and source evidence. Analytical severity supports prioritization and is not an official FDA severity determination. The default prepared observation snapshot uses deterministic rules. The newer observation contract uses a broad category with a more detailed theme. Unclassified or unsupported text should not be forced into a positive classification. Human review is required before consequential decisions.

title: Recurring risk methodology
keywords: recurrence recurring repeat repeated risk theme inspection grouping semantic
text: Recurring themes are assessed across distinct inspections. Repeated observation rows within the same inspection must not be counted as separate inspections. The legacy synthetic demo calculates repeats as distinct inspections minus one, clipped at zero. The current observation snapshot also groups similar wording using lexical similarity. A similarity group or recurring theme is an investigation lead, not proof of a repeated regulatory violation.

title: Risk scores and interpretation
keywords: risk scoring score calculate methodology weights rank site high prioritization
text: Site risk scores are deterministic weighted prioritization measures calculated by backend analytics using the configured methodology. Review the score components, scope and available denominators in the dashboard. A high score is a reason to inspect supporting evidence, not a finding of noncompliance. Missing data and insufficient coverage must remain visible. The model must not invent or recalculate a risk score from narrative text.

title: Real and synthetic datasets
keywords: dataset real synthetic demo FDA 483 provenance records mock pandas
text: The project contains real observation sources and a separate synthetic demonstration workflow. The synthetic demo includes 72 independently authored observations inspired by public FDA 483 formats. These examples are not authentic FDA findings and their expected labels are developer fixtures, not expert ground truth. The synthetic workflow uses pandas; the current large-dataset dashboard primarily uses SQL aggregation. Inspection counts and observation counts refer to different units and must not be combined.

title: Cleaning and evidence provenance
keywords: clean cleaning normalization deduplication duplicate null missing data quality evidence provenance source
text: Data engineering maps source fields into canonical records, normalizes values and records rejected and duplicate rows. Unknown values are preserved rather than invented. Inspection and observation records retain source identifiers, filenames or source references and row locators where available. Evidence should be inspected together with dataset scope, dates and known denominators. A model answer is an explanation of retrieved evidence, not a replacement for the original record.

title: Local operation, latency and evaluation
keywords: privacy security latency speed retrieval evaluation deepeval cache local ollama
text: The chatbot sends its bounded evidence context only to a loopback Ollama service on this computer. Dashboard calculations stay in the backend. Evidence is displayed before model generation finishes, and the UI reports retrieval and total answer timing. Source-ID and numeric-token checks catch some unsupported outputs but do not prove every statement correct. Human review remains necessary. Automated tests and deterministic evaluation metrics are not a substitute for expert-reviewed held-out question-and-answer evaluation.
